title: org-route-precedence-shadowing-causes-silent-allow-leak
creator: Ethan Morales
description:
Summary:
During recent traffic spikes we observed that certain requests from multi-route customers were allowed despite an explicit route-level deny and exhausted quota tokens for downstream tenants. Root cause analysis shows a policy-compile / cache-keying bug where compiled policies for an org-route combination are incorrectly reused across route aliases and tenant policy epochs. The result is a transient 'silent allow' where enforcement leapt to a cached allow decision and skipped proper accounting, causing under-throttling and billing reconciliation gaps.

Impact:
- Affected ~12 enterprise tenants (identified by Sentry alerts) with multi-route mappings and active route aliasing.
- Observed under-throttling for bursts: peak allowed throughput 2-4x expected for ~5-30s windows.
- Invoice reconciliation shows missing per-route meter entries for the affected windows (partial undercount).

Scope:
- Policy evaluation path (policy-compiler -> cache -> evaluator) for hierarchical rules (org-level, route-level, per-key overrides).
- Triggered when: route aliasing is enabled + concurrent policy update for the org + policy cache TTL not expired.

Desired outcome:
- Fix the cache-keying so compiled policy objects include canonical route id, tenant policy epoch/version, and route alias fingerprint. Add regression tests and an e2e smoke verifying accounting and enforcement on synthetic multi-route traffic. Roll out as a canary in runtime-1.23, monitor for missing meter entries and throttle-rate anomalies.
repro_steps: 1) Create org with two routes R1 and R1_alias that map to the same canonical handler.
2) Configure org-level allow for a broad token bucket and route-level deny for R1_alias.
3) Deploy a concurrent policy update (simulate new policy version) while sending steady traffic to R1_alias.
4) Observe enforcement logs: cached compiled policy id reused across alias boundary and evaluator emits ALLOW without accounting debit.
5) Check meter ingestion: missing per-route debit lines and downstream quota not decremented as expected.
observed_evidence: sample-log: evaluator.trace_id=7a3c... evaluator.result=ALLOW cache_key=org:1234|route:canonical:/v1/generate|epoch:42 (should have been epoch:43)
technical_notes: Root cause: cache key computed from (org_id, route_pattern) but route alias normalization occurs after cache lookup; when aliases are in play two distinct route inputs collapse to the same canonical key only in some timing windows, leading to stale compiled policy reuse.
Race scenario: concurrent policy update increments tenant policy epoch; compiler writes new compiled policy but TTL-based cache can still return old compiled object if epoch not included in the key.
Secondary issue: evaluator short-circuits accounting for 'fastpath allow' when compiled policy metadata indicates stateless allow; compiled metadata is stale and does not reflect route-level deny.
proposed_fix: 1) Change cache key to include (org_id, canonical_route_id, policy_epoch, alias_fingerprint) so any policy change or alias mapping invalidates old entries. 2) Tighten compiler invariants: attach a signed metadata blob to compiled policy with version and checksumming to validate on lookup. 3) Add audit-level fallback: if evaluator sees a mismatch between request route fingerprint and compiled metadata, force a recompile instead of fastpath allow. 4) Add unit + integration tests and a synthetic e2e harness covering aliasing + concurrent updates.
acceptance_criteria: No silent-allow reproduction in synthetic e2e for 10k requests across alias patterns.
Automated unit tests added to policy-compiler repo covering cache-key permutations.
Canary rollout (5% runtime capacity) shows zero increase in missing-meter alerts over 48h.
Billing reconciliation job shows no undercount deltas attributable to cache reuse in the affected window post-deploy.
rollout_plan:
- Implement fix behind feature flag (policy_cache_strict_keying).
- Run integration tests in CI.
- Deploy to canary cluster (runtime-1.23-canary). Monitor grafana_slo/rate-limiter, sentry alerts, and billing missing-meter job.
- After 48h with no regressions, ramp to 50% then 100%.
- Revoke feature flag only if regressions surface.
rollback_plan:
- Toggle feature flag off to restore prior cache semantics for immediate rollback.
- If toggling fails, revert runtime image to last known good (runtime-1.22) and run reconciliation job to identify affected windows.

2026-02-25 / Heather (PM): flagged two paying customers impacted; asked for expedited canary and communication plan to CSMs.
2026-03-02 / Security: reviewed change; no PII change, security_review_required=false but we should add audit logs for recompiles.
2026-03-08 / Review: internal code review found an extra mutex contention risk; opted for lock-free fingerprint comparison + double-check recompile to reduce latency impact.

Add e2e harness case for alias + concurrent update (owner: Androidev infra team, point-of-contact: Marco).
Prepare canary dashboard and alert thresholds for missing-meter deltas and throttle anomalies (owner: Observability).
